statement.p: Consider numbers of the form \alpha = a_1a_2a_3\dots a_n\text{,} with n digits, each digit from the set {\left\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\right\}}\text{.} For example, if n = 4, the number \alpha = a_1a_2a_3a_4 will have 4 digits from the set {\left\{1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8\right\}}\text{.}

li.p: How many such numbers are there?
How many such numbers are there for which the sum of the digits is even?
How many such numbers contain more even digits than odd digits?
8^{10} \cdot 4 numbers (choose any digits for the first 10 digits, then pick either an even or an odd last digit to make the sum even).

We need 6 or more even digits. 6 even digits: {11 \choose 6}4^6 4^{11-6}\text{.} 6+1 even digits: {11 \choose (6+1)}4^{6+1} *4^{11-6-1}\text{,} etc. By adding these together, we get the total number of ways to have 6 or more even digits.
